summary_responses.response: The Department of the Treasury’s Fiscal Service has issued a final rule amending the Uniform Offering Circular (UOC) for marketable Treasury bills, notes, and bonds to update definitions and terminology and to align with a planned auction system upgrade. The final rule is effective October 15, 2026, with the noncompetitive bid changes applying to auctions conducted under the upgraded system, and it is exempt from notice-and-comment requirements under the Administrative Procedure Act.

summary_responses.response: Cloud microservices often miscoordinate, leading to overloads and transaction rejections that disproportionately harm high‑value requests and enable attackers to exploit low‑value traffic spikes. Existing retry mechanisms fail to prioritize critical work and can trigger retry storms that amplify load and waste resources. DiffTry is a lightweight, stateless, distributed mechanism that assigns different retry limits to priority classes, turning retries into a rejection‑prioritization control without requiring overload detection or service coordination. The authors develop an analytical model for single and multi‑service networks, proving convergence and uniqueness for DAG topologies, and validate the approach through simulations and a live Kubernetes deployment. DiffTry can be deployed as a drop‑in service‑mesh plugin, requiring no code changes, and significantly lowers high‑priority rejection rates while improving throughput under both normal and overload conditions.

key_fact_breakdown.key_fact: DiffTry (Differential Retries) is a stateless mechanism that assigns different retry-attempt limits to different priority classes of requests to achieve differentiation in rejection rates.
Under overload with DiffTry, high-priority requests achieve a rejection rate of around 15% and account for about 85% of successful completions when both classes contribute 50% of input load.
DiffTry requires neither overload sensing nor microservices coordination and is implemented as a drop-in service-mesh plugin requiring no application code changes.

The paper develops an analytical model for DiffTry starting with two services in tandem, then generalizes it to networks of services using an open-network model combined with flow classes and priorities.

The paper proves that network-wide class-level success rates increase monotonically with retry limits and validates the analysis on a live Kubernetes deployment where measured rejection closely matches the theoretical predictions.

summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) issued a direct final rule amending its Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) regulations to reflect statutory changes enacted in January 2021 and December 2023. The revisions broaden FMLA eligibility by counting virtually all federal civilian service—including temporary and intermittent work—and honorable active military service in the Army, Navy, Air Force, Space Force, or Marine Corps toward the 12‑month service requirement. The rule also permits employees to substitute annual or sick leave earned under non‑title 5 authorities for unpaid FMLA leave and removes coverage for Veterans Health Administration employees who are covered by a separate VA leave system. The changes codify prior OPM guidance and align the regulations with the amended statutes, ensuring consistency with the Federal Employee Paid Leave Act and paid parental leave provisions. The rule is effective December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, 2026, in which case OPM may withdraw the affected provisions.
